name: urgent-referral-stemi
note: Canonical positive: realistic synthetic urgent-referral letter (invented patient, no learner text). Anchor for route + guard + criteria + verify calibration. criteria ranges sit on the OFFICIAL descriptor scale the pilot now uses (JevWritingPilot.Criteria): c1_purpose 0-3 (four levels), c2..c6 0-7 (one level per score). The request to the reader is made in the LAST paragraph, so the official 'immediately clear' Purpose descriptor keeps c1 below the top level: the c1 range only requires that purpose is not judged unclear (>= 1). The pass-level c1 anchor (purpose stated in the opening) lives in writing-outcome.json.

state.letter:
Dear Dr Aisha Rahman,

Re: Mr Kenneth Osei, DO 14 March 1958

Mr Osei attended today reporting a two-day history of central chest pain, radiating to his left jaw, associated with sweating and nausea. The pain began at rest and lasted approximately forty minutes. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes and takes metformin 1g twice daily.

On examination he appeared pale and clammy. Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg, pulse 96 regular, oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Heart sounds normal, chest clear. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF.

I suspect an inferior STEMI. I have given aspirin 300mg orally and admit him to the acute medical unit. Please review him urgently regarding primary PCI, as the cardiology registrar is currently unavailable.

verify.claim: The letter names the recipient clinician.
The letter reports an ECG showing ST elevation.
The letter reports that today's ECG was normal.
